synthesis.overnight_summary: Gold held up through the MCX close (spot $4,137.94 at 23:42 IST; GC Dec settled $4,150) as US yields eased, but a fatal drone strike near Aramco's Shaybah field and the US order for non-emergency staff to leave Saudi Arabia pushed Brent back above $110 overnight. The market read the escalation as inflation-and-Fed-hike risk rather than a haven bid, and spot slid ~1% through $4,100 to ~$4,090-4,098 in Asia, with silver down 2-3%. The rupee opened steady at 94.47, so the model gap was almost all COMEX (Rs -1434), putting fair value at Rs 144622; MCX Dec's first prints near 144,550 (low 144,467) matched that within Rs 72, so the open was aligned. Since then the rupee has weakened to ~94.80 on oil, which cushions MCX (live fair ~Rs 144827) even as spot keeps sliding. For today, MCX is trading below its 200-DEMA with oil, yields and the 28-Oct FOMC the main drivers; US jobless claims at 18:00 IST are the next catalyst.
